utterances.text: The legal organs of authority in the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please, what they are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you very clearly. Until the 17th of April, 1992, it was the municipal assembly of Konjic, the council for national defence of the municipality and the crisis staff of the municipality. After the 17th of April, 1992, it became the war presidency of the municipality as a substitute for the municipal assembly. Those were the legal organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this happened well before -- well, it happened before the 17th of April, so it was the municipality, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even before the 17th of April, we had legal organs. As of the 6th of April, in view of the fact that the war had started, according to the municipal statute and according to the constitution, a crisis staff was formed and a council for national defence which functioned until the 17th of April, 1992. After the last assembly meeting, the war presidency of the municipality started to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, when the military activities started in and around the Konjic municipality, the military activity especially perpetrated by the Serb paramilitary or the JNA was designed to cut Konjic off from Sarajevo, in particular, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to isolate Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the final analysis to occupy it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, Sarajevo was itself preoccupied with the conflict that it had on its hands; you would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, wouldn't you, that when confronted with this military conflict that ensued in the early part of 1992, April of 1992, there was much to be done to adjust the municipal structures and bodies in order to prepare itself for the anticipated and ensuing conflict; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The legal bodies of the municipality of Konjic, even under conditions of peace, had plans which envisaged how those legal bodies would behave in emergencies such as a situation of imminent threat of war or war. That is what the legal authorities did in accordance with their competencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those plans envisage and deal as their topic with a situation, whereby the JNA would turn on its own people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They assumed any kind of emergency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the outset of the conflict, I take it that you would consider the HVO to be part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't quite consider it because, the HVO as a structure was not envisaged by positive, legal regulations of Bosnia-Herzegovina in times of peace. But, in view of the fact that this was a special form of organisation, of a part of the people of Konjic municipality, and in view of the fact that they had the same goals, in the sense of defending the municipality of Konjic, the legal bodies of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina recognised them as an integral part of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were they so recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I put it to you that it wasn't until sometime later that the HVO was accepted as a force that could work with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you wouldn't disagree with that, would you? Perhaps I'll withdraw that. Initially, the HVO was accepted as part of the defence forces, at least so far as the Konjic municipality was concerned, because they supported your aims in the conflict, didn't they? You had the same aims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what he has already said, they were joining us in defending Konjic so they were treated as legal organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it didn't matter about their foundation, legal foundation or whether they were a valid, legal force within the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina or within the municipality of Konjic, did it? It was because they supported your military aims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was very important. It did matter because all their activities were in accordance with the activities of the legal institutions. And the armed forces of Konjic municipality, as is well-known and as I already said yesterday, already on May the 12th set up a joint command of the armed forces of Konjic municipality comprising the TO, the HVO and the ministry of the interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the HVO was, in fact, technically and a legal force, in the sense that it didn't have the force of law or support of law in either the constitution or the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina, then you would have had nothing to do with it, notwithstanding the fact that it would have participated in the war with you; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already said and I'm repeating that because of our common aims and because members of the HVO were citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, therefore, there was no reason not to establish such a relationship. They were not an illegal formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it had nothing to do with the legality, did it; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not envisaged in the plans and documents. They did not exist actually, as a form before the war, but they emerged as a self-organised military force of the Croatian people and they joined in the struggle against the aggression, against the internationally recognised Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there is nothing unclear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have agreed with this force had it attacked you? If the HVO would have attacked you, would you have agreed that it was a legal entity within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is that really relevant? You see, in a situation like that, in a situation where the municipal defence is situated, they would even go to the Devil to seek his help. They would not bother about the legal position. That was the force available to them to help them, so they joined them. They treated them as a legal force.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The witness agrees absolutely, and that's exactly the point I was trying to get to, Your Honour. I thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our lives were in jeopardy. We were defending our biological existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. And you would have done anything to defend yourselves, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that has been taken for granted all along.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps it shouldn't have been, Your Honours, with respect, because the whole argument of this defence is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not quite everything, not quite anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the primary responsibility was not to sort out the fine points of law, when it comes to defending the municipality of Konjic, was it? It was to defend the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to this whole line of questioning. It's, I think, pretty irrelevant. I don't see how any of this has anything to do with what happened in Celebici or what didn't happen in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I join in the objection because the witness already said that it was a constitutional obligation of every citizen to defend the country, and the HVO members were also citizens of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I assure Your Honours that the relevance of this line of cross-examination will become crystal clear in due course, and I can assure you, that in no way, is it irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, because of the unusual situation of not having the JNA there and having the Territorial Defence and the HVO, it became necessary to set up a joint command, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in order to coordinate our joint defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in part, that was as a consequence of the fact that the HVO's command was separate from that of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said, I said yesterday and I think today too that these three parts of the armed forces, the three elements comprising the armed forces of the Konjic Municipality, had a different chains of command: members of the MUP were accountable to the ministry of the interior; members of the TO were under the subordination of the TO staff and HVO members were subordinated to their command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the war presidency were concerned, were they not, to ensure that maximum efficiency was achieved by the joint efforts of both the TO and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal presidency had no jurisdiction in terms of the control and command over the armed forces. I said that already yesterday. But as a body, it is -- had a series of responsibilities within the system of defence, but never within the system of control and command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you anything about command and control and at all, doctor. My question was, that the war presidency was concerned to ensure that you -- you achieved the maximum efficiency out of both of these forces? It's a yes/no answer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our aim was to ensure the maximum efficiency of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that, the achievement of that efficiency was a little difficult at times because of differences that developed between the HVO and the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the joint command of the armed forces of the Municipality of Konjic was formed, I think there were no major differences because the commander of the joint command came from the TO and the chief of staff of the command came from the HVO. So there were no significant differences at the beginning. They emerged later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that may so and I don't quarrel with you about that. But it's true, is it not, that you saw the need to consolidate how these military forces were to operate? And when I say "you", I am talking of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representatives of the armed forces insisted on this and it was their job to do that. And the presidency could only receive reports about those activities by representatives of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you suggesting that it wasn't a concern or a responsibility of the war presidency, this issue of bringing together the two forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not the concrete job of the war presidency, but the war presidency was briefed on all the activities that they engaged in, but only in the sense of briefings, information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the decision was made to appoint Zejnil Delalic as a coordinator, that's right, wasn't it, by the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 18th of May, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a decision, I think, that was made by the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by you, the actual document of appointment was made by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The actual document, I didn't make it, but the appropriate services made it. We already noted that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you signed it, though?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, his function was to coordinate between the war presidency and between the HVO and the TO, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the ministry of the interior. The three segments of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. And the object of that exercise was to achieve maximum efficiency, was it not, in the military forces that you had available to you at the time, for the defence of the Municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The aim was to achieve maximum efficiency in the relationship between the war presidency and the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll accept that. But don't you agree with me that by achieving maximum efficiency in the relationship, one would hope there would flow from that, maximum efficiency of effort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree entirely, perhaps we have different views of this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll disagree on that. Now, doctor, the achievement of efficiency between, or communication between the three groups, the TO, the HVO and the MUP, you would agree, wouldn't you, that the ultimate objective of that was your defence, the defence of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that the defence of the municipality is primarily a military matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency as a civilian body had a whole series of responsibilities within the system of defence, so I wouldn't agree with you entirely, even though it was not a military body, it still had a series of responsibilities within the sphere of defence as stipulated by the constitution and the law. But the actual combat activities, the control and command, was carried out by the responsible military bodies. That part of their activities depended, in some areas, on the activities of the economic staff and other bodies which were purely civilian. And, therefore, also on the activities of the war presidency and its coordinator who were civilian persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the reality is, isn't it, doctor, that there was a sharing of responsibility in relation to the military effort of defence of the municipality? Now surely that's not an extraordinary proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody was discharging his responsibilities in accordance with his jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we can only assume that. You're not saying that you know that as a fact, when you use the word "everybody", are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the persons who held certain positions had certain competencies and they acted accordingly at a given moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at times some people who didn't have those competencies did other things which didn't fall within them, but if it suited the defence of the municipality, that wouldn't have been extraordinary or unacceptable, would it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Give him some definite instance, your question is too general for him to answer. Give him some instance. The way you put the question is too general for him to answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the City of Konjic, and this is a hypothetical example, if the City of Konjic was under attack and action needed to be taken to put out a fire, if people from a nearby building came out and attempted to put out the fire rather than the fire brigade, that wouldn't be regarded as extraordinary or exceptional, would it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I object to these hypothetical questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We had a series of them earlier Your Honour, and there seemed to be no objection to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That wouldn't be outside neighbours coming in and putting out a fire, would not be something not expected of the neighbours, so that would hardly be a good example to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I apologise for my example, Your Honour, it's the best I could think of at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If, for example, members of the war presidency, or officials appointed by the war presidency, became involved in the exchange of prisoners in Celebici, we're dealing with prisoners in Celebici; that wouldn't necessarily be an extraordinary circumstance in the time, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, doctor, when you first spoke -- well, I think it's the first time you spoke to the officer of the Prosecutor, Mr. D'Hooge, in the 31st of April, 1996. On that occasion, you say you didn't know who appointed Zejnil Delalic as coordinator, why did you say that at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will be very clear, my first interview in 1996 was ad hoc and a long time had elapsed since the events in question and if there is any collision or imprecision, it could be attributed to the long time that had passed since those events. But I made another statement to your investigator and he reminded me of those things in that second interview, so that I explained all those facts if anything was unclear to the investigator of this honourable Tribunal. On the other hand, if anyone casts any doubt as to what I am saying today, after all I am under oath, there are additional documents that I have submitted to this Tribunal, such as the videotape of the assembly meeting and me speaking at that meeting and all the conclusions reached. And they may be placed at the court's disposal. So that I think that in my second interview, I explained all the facts that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only reason I ask the question that it's somewhat extraordinary, that someone that you yourself appointed is not something that you would know about when questioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not unusual. You see, I have gone through a very difficult period. You must understand that a long time has gone by and I spoke to the investigator ad hoc. I was eager to assist this honourable Tribunal as I am now. And I think that I clarified in my second statement all the facts that you are now referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well, at the same time, as you said you didn't know who appointed him you said, and I'll quote directly: "The function of coordinator must be a military function?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not a soldier, you see, I am a doctor by profession. Therefore, I may have been imprecise, which could have been attributable either to a misunderstanding of the question or possibly an error in the translation. I think that in many sentences, there was imprecision in the translation. But I think there's no doubt that I clarified all those points in my second statement, given to the same gentleman that is to this Tribunal. Allow me, after all I refreshed my memory, I haven't been prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you check that? Did you go away and check whether or not, in fact, it was merely a translation error? Because you audio recorded the interview yourself, didn't you, on your own personal equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't consider it to be important to check. I had the oral promise of the investigator that he would send me copies. I didn't receive them, but I think that isn't important because I explained everything in my second testimony and here I am now. In any case, I think this testimony today is the most important one because I am testifying under oath. Those statements at the time were not of such a nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second interview that you gave to the Prosecutor's officer, again, Mr. D'Hooge and on this occasion, Mr. McLeod, were you corrected the question of the appointment of Zejnil Delalic as coordinator, and corrected your previous statement. That was given on the 4th of February, 1997 and after you had spoken to Ms. Residovic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke briefly. I told the investigator when he asked me whether I had communicated with any one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told him that you had spoken to Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a short interview, oral interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was then that you emphasised the fact that the function of the coordinator was a civilian one and not a military one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now why was Zejnil Delalic appointed as the coordinator? Why did you appoint him as coordinator? You and the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was also Zejnil Delalic was also authorised to, in a logistics capacity, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he discharged certain duties in procuring supplies, material, technical supplies, for the needs of the defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that included heavy military supplies, and when I use the word "heavy", I mean in terms of ammunitions and methods by which you could wage war, not only soft materials, such as clothes and food?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I didn't hear Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He also provided certain communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And communications, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these were communications, equipment, uniform, but I would disagree with you and I don't know what the term heavy military supplies implies, but as far as ammunition is concerned, there was no need for it at the time because the factory of ammunitions in Konjic was put under the control of the legal authorities of Konjic and after a certain time, we also normally activated the production there for the needs of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not very expert in weapons and matters of that nature --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Neither am I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if he purchased military equipment -- I'll have to come back to that. Do you know whether or not he purchased military equipment such as rocket launchers and guns and things of that nature, when he was in Croatia or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic was authorised by a special authorisation, which I mentioned before, he was appointed coordinator. I explained all of this yesterday. And his trip to Zagreb, aimed at providing, procuring those military supplies. I think I was very clear yesterday and this was the special authorisation which I reviewed yesterday. But all those activities stemmed from the conclusions of the war presidency, regarding supplies and distribution of supplies and equipment. And they did not relate to anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, perhaps you might look at the document, which is prosecution Exhibit 99-7-4. So it's not a prosecution exhibit, I apologise -- okay, 99-7-4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the document I saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said that it did not give you any military function. That's your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you can see everything from the preamble of that document. This is an authorisation based on the decision by the war presidency regarding equipping and supplying and distribution of this material and nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says in paragraph 3, does it not, "All kinds of agreements on possible joint actions of troops from other areas and theatres of operation in our area and theatre of operation and vice versa," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not and every point can be interpreted exclusively in the light of the preamble of that document, and this is my interpretation and I don't interpret it in any other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. But will you agree with me, and I'm not asking you to agree with whatever interpretation you think I'm putting on it, but merely to agree with me, that it says in paragraph 3: "All kinds of agreements on possible joint actions of troops from other areas and theatres of operations in our area and theatre of operation and vice versa"?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. The witness has just said that he interprets this in light of the preamble.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I press the question. I'm simply asking whether he agrees with me that that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything that figures in the document stems from the preamble of the document and that is all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I will ask you to do something for me. Will you please read paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "All forms of agreement about possible joint actions of troops from other zones and theatres of operations in other areas and on our own and vice versa."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that is a task that is given to him by the war presidency, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in accordance with the preamble of the document in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a task that was given to him, both by yourself and by Captain Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't given to you by Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The signature of Captain Ramic, I explained by the fact that Mr. Delalic was a military -- and as a civilian, he could not leave, actually the area, without permission. The orders he received were not from Captain Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was actually a military, so please correct that error. The transcript says that Mr. Delalic was a soldier but what it should say is he was of military age. I apologise, but in English I see again the word "soldier" and that is not something that the witness has said. The witness said that he was subject to conscription in the sense that he could be mobilised for military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic also provided his house in Konjic, in support of the military effort of Konjic to defend itself, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, as far as I know, did give part of his house to accommodate the municipal communications staff headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that communications function assisted the military effort, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the municipal communications centre of the municipal TO staff, and Mr. Delalic just allowed them to use a certain part of his private home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the document we looked at a moment ago, and in your evidence you've spoken of Mr. Delalic having a logistics function. A logistics function is a military function, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All people who obtained any resources and who assisted the defence, according to you, would then be soldiers, but that is not true. Mr. Delalic at that point in time was a civilian. But through his activities, he managed to procure certain resources for the needs of the defence, but those activities do not make him a soldier. Such activities were engaged in by other people too. Other people were given such authorisations too. It was not only for Mr. Delalic. All the people who could be of assistance at the time, would be given by us this kind of authorisation as evidence so that they didn't have to be soldiers and that was the case here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, considering you appointed Mr. Delalic to the position of coordinator, I take it that that would make you his superior, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic was a coordinator and this is a function that we have clearly explained yesterday. He was a man, a mediator, a communicator between the joint command of the armed forces and the war presidency or, rather, the economic staff or certain parts of that body. He would reflect the needs of these bodies and nothing more than that. In any event, those were his duties which didn't place him in a position of a person who could independently make decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Should I take that as a "yes" or a "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not independent in decision making.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was: Seeing as you appointed him as coordinator, did that make you his superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the sense that you imply, but it makes him accountable for the tasks that he received from the war presidency, and he had to submit appropriate reports to the body that appointed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was his superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it was the economic staff, if he was given a task by the economic staff as a civilian body, then he would be accountable to the economic staff. And if he received a task from the civil defence, then he would report to that body. Therefore, the war presidency, as a body, had a wide range of segments headed by various people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the economic staff and the civilian defence all came under the war presidency, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The civil defence and the economic staff were component parts in the structure of the municipal assembly or the war presidency as civilian bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were president of the war presidency and prior to that president of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're using a term that was customary at the time. The real name of the body --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: For example, Delalic has appointed Ms. Residovic as his counsel. Does she become his superior? He says he was just acting as a go-between, acting as a link between the two organisations. There's no question of any superiority. This is what his position is. He submits reports, but the bodies to which he submits these reports is not his superior. As I said, Delalic has appointed Madam Residovic as his counsel. She doesn't become his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the jurisdiction that I was formerly practising law, whenever I acted for a client, I had to obey their instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But there was no relationship of superiority and subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm merely getting to the point as to who gave him instructions and who he had to report to. I got part of the question, but I'll move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that Mr. Delalic had to make reports to you, in his position as coordinator; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In any event, to the war presidency or to the body that gave him an assignment, not to me personally, but, yes, if he was given an assignment by a particular department, then he would report to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what reports did he make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes these were oral reports and sometimes in writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the subject matter of them were? I know it's been a long time ago, but if you could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only dealing with what his task was, the specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you recall any of the subject matters of the reports that he made, what he reported to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember on one occasion there was a large delivery of flour coming from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he told you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because these supplies would be coming in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of the military equipment and that that he had acquired in his logistics capacity, did he tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The joint command of the armed forces did have a department called assistant commander for logistics, and Mr. Kevric was in charge of this department. So any materials that arrived in Konjic, if they were a part of the military equipment or communications equipment, had to be taken over by the responsible military bodies. And Delalic would just say that they had arrived, but he would not, under any circumstances, be responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever communicate with you about taking receipt of logistics material that he had acquired? I'm speaking particularly about the period of time when --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was not necessary because there were people and bodies that were responsible for this. And the war presidency is a civilian body, so it was not within its terms of reference to enter into such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may be a question of a translation or interpretation. Just a moment, please. LiveNote, page 81, line 11, I believe I heard the witness say "Kevric" and it came across "Krevic." Perhaps that could be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Kevric. He was the responsible person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, do you know a person by the name of Mr. Sinik, and I'll spell that because I may not have pronounced it properly, S-I-N-I-K?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think you mispronounced it. It doesn't mean anything, what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I've spelled it. I'll spell it slowly again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In our language, it doesn't fit somehow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The English, and I may have it wrong, S-I-N-I-K?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think his name is "Joko ^ Sinik." Do you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's a person who claims to have known you for 20 years, but you don't know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot decipher. I cannot recollect. I cannot find him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He apparently had a weekend house which was close to your house. Does that help you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a house at all. I have an apartment in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, would you agree that, on occasions, the war presidency and the Territorial Defence gave joint orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you clarify the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Were there occasions when joint orders were issued by both the war presidency and the Territorial Defence or the commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency could only issue orders as envisaged by law, and if the signature of a commander appeared on the document, as I just explained, using the previous document, that was just the sign of, perhaps, permission to men of military age to be able to leave the municipality, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you might look at a document for me, Defence Exhibit D144 Va/18. I do apologise. I will repeat that. It's Exhibit D144 Va/8. Just look at this document for me, would you, please? Is that your signature that appears at the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is very clear. I'll be glad to explain it and why it is like this. Actually, the war presidency, within the framework of its competencies, set up Radio Konjic. In view of the fact that we were at war, it was quite normal, customary for information to be censored.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to assist everyone in the court, could you put the English version of it on the overhead projector and then everyone can see what we're talking about. Just put the English version there for me, please. Just put it on the projector. I'm sorry to have interrupted you, Doctor. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document has to do with the activities of Radio Konjic, and Radio Konjic is an institution founded by the war presidency. And in view of its significance in the system of defence, certain information could not be broadcast over the same radio and that is why this paper was signed by the commander on the censorship of any reports of a military nature that could be used by the enemy. That is how I explained this, so nothing more than that. It has to do with the functioning of Radio Konjic as an information media, as a media institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, having said all of that, you would agree with me that it's a joint order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not a joint order. It is a document providing for the possibility for some kind of control over information of a military nature and which, if broadcast, would harm the defence of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the word in the middle of the -- will you tell me what it says in the very middle of the top of the page under the heading where it says "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Konjic Municipality War Presidium," and then there's a word typed in the middle of the page. What is that word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which word? I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the word at the top of the page that says "Order"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It doesn't say "I order." It says, "It is ordered," and the order refers to a civilian institution, Radio Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was whether it was an order. It says that it's an order. It looks like an order. It acts like an order. Surely it's an order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I explained yesterday we had the right to give orders to bodies which we founded, that is, administrative bodies or other institutions that we had founded and radio Konjic was an institution founded by the war presidency, and according to the municipal statute, article 66, we were entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for a minor intervention. I think the Bosnian version should be put on ELMO too. I don't see the heading, the word "order," that is seen in the translation. There may be an error in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would you translate that word in English, that Bosnian word in English? How would you translate that word, that Bosnian word into English?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but the text in Bosnian does not contain that word and I just wish to draw your attention to this. I am not a translator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't think it really matters. It depends on the institution issuing the order. If it's a civilian institution issuing the order, it doesn't have the same effect as a military institution. They are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour, for the truth of its contents, having it been recognised.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness did not recognise it, he recognised the document without the heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is his document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is his document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but addressed to a civilian body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is his document, but he didn't recognise the English translation in which the heading is "Order". In the Bosnian version there's no such heading. That is the only difference. Because this heading doesn't exist in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So tender the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender both, Your Honour, and note that it's not my translation, it's Madam Residovic's translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, were you aware that, in addition to authorisations given to Mr. Delalic by you and by Mr. Ramic, he also had authorisation to conclude certain agreements based on authorisations that he received directly from the ministry of defence in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with your statement. He received authorisations from the war presidency and not from Mr. Ramic. He could be given just permission from Ramic to go away, being subject to conscription. At the same time, I must say that I do know that he had such authorisations, some such authorisations, what in particular, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he -- really the point of my question was not about Mr. Ramic, but whether or not he had authorisations from the ministry of defence in Sarajevo, that you knew about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He says yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not sure what he said yes to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said he was authorised, but he doesn't know in respect of what matters. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question is unclear. I really don't know what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, it may resolve itself this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at Exhibit P-235. Now, doctor, just looking at that particular document, and perhaps you might put the English version on the overhead projector so their Honours can see and the Defence can see what we're talking about. Would you do that for me? Now that's a document signed by Minister Jerko Doko, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's issued by the ministry of defence in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point I am asking you, were you aware of this authorisation that was given to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency was not a body that was required to send out such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I am asking you is, when you read this document, you see that it gives Mr. Delalic authorisation, by the ministry of defence in Sarajevo, to conclude agreements on mutual exchanges of equipment, et cetera, do you see that? Now all I am asking you is, were you aware of this authorisation in your capacity as president of the war presidency? A simple yes or no will do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at the moment it was issued, I was not aware of this because it may not address the body of which I was in charge, so there was no reason that I had to know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you subsequently informed about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's the first time I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So, it's true then, obviously, that Mr. Delalic may have had authorisations and powers that you, yourself, did not know about, even at the time or even now, indeed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not agree with you, with that statement. I am only sure that Mr. Delalic was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- Change his status.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I wouldn't press it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I think you testified to the fact that the war presidency formed a commission which had the responsibility of settling matters of people who were killed or injured or missing, did you testify as to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's referring to that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, such a commission did exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Jasna Dzumhur was appointed as the chairperson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vice-president of that commission, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from its duties and obligations, it was required to keep records of its work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were directly accountable to the same body, state body, a central state body in Sarajevo. And occasionally they would submit reports about their work and about the activities of the war presidency. But the superior body was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the superior body in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it still exists, chaired by Mr. Masovic, it is a state body dealing with missing persons, I think. I think that is the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's that called? Do you know it's name? It doesn't matter if you don't, but if you know it's name it might help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the details, but I think it is the commission in Sarajevo chaired by Mr. Masovic. I think it was -- it's referred to as a state commission for the missing persons or something to that effect. In any case, it did exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a military body or a civilian body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it is a civilian body, not a military body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said a moment ago, a few minutes ago, that that sometimes you received reports from this commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Jasna Dzumhur was an official of the municipal assembly of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any reports on people that had died in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember having received such reports, but if there were such reports, the servers of -- there was a special service dealing with this and it was able to communicate with a service of persons on -- actual funeral services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you receive any reports from the funeral services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The funeral service was in charge of this and I think that all the institutions were, in some way, under the obligation to submit reports on their work to the municipal assembly of Konjic, or, in other words, to the war presidency, because these were all basically civilian bodies. And the commission on funeral services, I think it was part of a company of an enterprise. I don't know if it was the public utilities enterprise, it was a service within that company, which dealt with the burial of persons, of dead persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember receiving reports on people who had been buried, who died in Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that, I know that some people had died, but I cannot remember the details at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how it was said that they died? What they died of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, and on the basis of the information I have had, that those were people who suffered from serious chronicle diseases, diabetes, heart diseases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we'll have to have a break here and return at 4.30. Now when we return at 4.30, we intend to have a status conference on the problems of -- because signing the witnesses and the duplications we've been having on witness' lists. And we'll deal with that at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, should the witness wait until after the status conference or can he be discharged? Your Honours, should the witness wait until after the status conference or should he be discharged for the moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The witness can wait to be discharged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cross-examination is not finished. Wait to be discharged.
